Sierpc Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sierpc, Poland

Not demolished. A Jewish community existed in Sierpc no later than 1739; by 1910, 3,895 Jews lived there, declining slightly to 2,861 (43%) by 1921 before most were murdered at Treblinka and Auschwitz-Birkenau. The cemetery's existence is first recorded in 1775. Germans used its tombstones to reinforce roads during WWII; Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1961. Despite restoration efforts led by Sierpc descendants and Rabbi Eliakim Schlesinger of the Committee for the Preservation of Jewish Cemeteries in Europe - including recovering matzevot, partial fencing, and cleaning - the site remains in poor condition today, with a football field built directly on the grounds. In 2009, the cemetery's historic wooden mortuary, one of the last surviving examples of wooden Jewish material culture in Europe, collapsed.
